title: From API Request to Business Result
readerIntent: Follow a typical secured operation through Nodics layers.
owner: Owning business module plus shared request, pipeline, data, and security capabilities
summary: A route enters the governed request pipeline, resolves identity and context, delegates through controller and service layers, uses authoritative models, and returns normalized status and trace context.

sections.heading: Example flow
items: The router matches method and path and declares whether authentication is required.
The request pipeline resolves tenant, authentication, authorization, headers, and request context.
The controller validates transport-level input and delegates the use case.
A facade may coordinate several services; the owning service applies business rules.
Schema item or search models apply data contracts and use configured framework providers.
Interceptors run only at declared extension points; events publish facts after the owned state transition.
The response handler maps stable status codes and trace context to the transport response.

sections.heading: Failure behavior
items: Authentication, authorization, validation, conflict, provider, and internal failures retain distinct stable codes.
Pipeline error paths perform bounded cleanup and normalized response handling.
Logs and metrics include safe context and correlation without exposing credentials or sensitive records.

sections.heading: Deployment independence
paragraphs: The same logical flow can execute with modules in one local monoServer or across separately deployed module servers. Transport and resilience become topology concerns; capability ownership does not move.
